The formal definition is in Chap 3.9.5.2.1.2, Chap 3.9.6.1 (Table 34) of the S1000D specification and in the [S1000D Issue 7 data dictionary](https://users.s1000d.org/S1000D_DD_7/Files/attributes/internalRefTargetType.xml).
:::

`internalRefTargetType` is the attribute that states what type of target an `internalRef` (a reference inside the same data module) points to. It is optional.

## Elements that carry it

In the 33 XML schemas of Issue 7, 1 element carries this attribute.

| Element | Schemas | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `internalRef` | 28 | Optional |

## Allowed values

The allowed values are decided in two steps: by the XML schema and by BREX (Business Rules Exchange).

| Defined by | Content |
| --- | --- |
| XML schema | The type is `internalRefTargetTypeAttType` (based on `xs:string`). The values are an enumeration of 99 values, from `irtt01` to `irtt99` |
| Default BREX (BREX-S1-00204) | Allows 17 values (including ranges and patterns) for `//@internalRefTargetType`. The rule applies to all schemas |

Of the values in the XML schema enumeration, the 34 values `irtt17` to `irtt50` are not allowed by BREX-S1-00204. They pass XML schema validation, but they are violations in a check against the default BREX.

BREX-S1-00204 allows the following values and defines how a lower-level BREX can tailor each of them.

| Value | `valueForm` | `valueTailoring` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `irtt01` to `irtt16` | `single` | `lexical` |
| `irtt51~irtt99` | `range` | `restrictable` |

## In this stack

| Operation | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Read | [`read_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-data-module/). The value is in the reference of the `internalRef`, as written |
| Check that the target exists | [`check_references`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/check-references/). It checks that the `id` an `internalRef` points to is in the same data module |
| Check whether a value is allowed | [`lookup_value`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/brex/lookup-value/) |
